lessonRef.focus: conic equations and their geometric features
lessonRef.title: Discussion or problem seminar: conic equations and their geometric features

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: One approach is shown. There is at least one other that works.

items.prompt: Do an oblique and a right cylinder with the same base and height have equal volume?

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: For each, name a second method before you solve it.

items.prompt: A circle has radius 5 and centre O. A point P lies 13 from O. Explain the construction of a tangent from P and give the tangent length.
choices: Draw the perpendicular bisector of OP; the tangent length is 12.
Draw the circle centred at P with radius 5; the tangent length is 12.
Draw the circle on diameter OP; it meets the given circle at the point of tangency, and the tangent length is 8.
Draw the circle on diameter OP; it meets the given circle at the point of tangency, and the tangent length is 12.

items.prompt: An ellipse centred at the origin has foci at (±4, 0) and the sum of distances to the foci equal to 10. Write its equation.
A hyperbola centred at the origin has foci at (±5, 0) and the absolute difference of distances to the foci equal to 8. Write its equation.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Compare a cone and a cylinder with the same base and height. What does Cavalieri’s principle tell us?
choices: Nothing, because Cavalieri’s principle applies only to prisms.
The cone has one third the volume, which Cavalieri’s principle establishes by comparing cross-sections against a reference solid.
They have equal volumes, and matching cross-sections is exactly how the sphere volume formula is derived.
They have equal volumes, because every horizontal cross-section has the same area at the same height.

items.prompt: A circle has radius 8 and centre O. A point P lies 17 from O. Explain the construction of a tangent from P and give the tangent length.
choices: Draw the circle on diameter OP; it meets the given circle at the point of tangency, and the tangent length is 9.
Draw the circle centred at P with radius 8; the tangent length is 15.
Draw the circle on diameter OP; it meets the given circle at the point of tangency, and the tangent length is 15.
Draw the perpendicular bisector of OP; the tangent length is 15.

items.prompt: An ellipse centred at the origin has foci at (±6, 0) and the sum of distances to the foci equal to 20. Write its equation.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Argue for one method over another. Say what makes it better, not just that it is.

items.prompt: A hyperbola centred at the origin has foci at (±13, 0) and the absolute difference of distances to the foci equal to 10. Write its equation.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Compare an oblique cylinder and a right cylinder with the same base area and the same height. What does Cavalieri’s principle tell us?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
